lessons.title: Exercise 1.1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1: Identify each of the following as a rational or irrational number

(i) 2.353535 (ii) 0.6 (recurring) (iii) 2.236067... (iv) sqrt(7) (v) e (vi) pi (vii) 5 + sqrt(11) (viii) sqrt(3) + sqrt(13) (ix) 15/4 (x) (2 - sqrt(2))(2 + sqrt(2))

Rule: A number that can be written in the form p/q (p, q integers, q not 0) is rational. Terminating and non-terminating recurring decimals are rational; non-terminating non-recurring decimals are irrational.

(i) 2.353535: it is a terminating decimal, so it can be written in p/q form. Hence it is a rational number.

(ii) 0.666... is a non-terminating recurring decimal (6 repeats), so it is a rational number.

(iii) 2.236067... is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it cannot be written in p/q form. Hence it is an irrational number.

(iv) sqrt(7): 7 is not a perfect square, so sqrt(7) is non-terminating and non-recurring. Hence it is an irrational number.

(v) e = 2.71828182845904... is non-terminating and non-recurring. Hence it is an irrational number.

(vi) pi = 3.141592653589793... is non-terminating and non-recurring. Hence it is an irrational number.

(vii) 5 + sqrt(11): sqrt(11) is irrational, and rational + irrational = irrational. Hence 5 + sqrt(11) is an irrational number.

(viii) sqrt(3) + sqrt(13): both terms are irrational and their sum does not terminate or recur. Hence it is an irrational number.

(ix) 15/4 is already in p/q form with q = 4 (not 0). Hence it is a rational number.

(x) (2 - sqrt(2))(2 + sqrt(2)): Formula: (a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2.

Step 1: = (2)^2 - (sqrt(2))^2

Step 2: = 4 - 2

Step 3: = 2, which is in p/q form (2/1). Hence it is a rational number.

Q2: Represent the following numbers on the number line

(i) sqrt(2) (ii) sqrt(3) (iii) 4 1/3 (iv) -2 1/7 (v) 5/8 (vi) 2 3/4 [Construction described in words with all labels named; see flag in manifest]

(i) sqrt(2): Step 1: Draw a number line and mark point O at 0 and point A at 1, so OA = 1 unit.

Step 2: At A, draw AB perpendicular to the line with AB = 1 unit. Join O to B, forming right-angled triangle OAB.

Step 3: Formula (Pythagoras theorem): (OB)^2 = (OA)^2 + (AB)^2.

Step 4: (OB)^2 = (1)^2 + (1)^2 = 1 + 1 = 2, so OB = sqrt(2).

Step 5: With O as centre and radius OB = sqrt(2), draw an arc meeting the number line at P. Then OP = sqrt(2), so P represents sqrt(2).

(ii) sqrt(3): Step 1: First locate sqrt(2) at point P as in part (i), so OP = sqrt(2).

Step 2: At P, draw PQ perpendicular to the line with PQ = 1 unit. Join O to Q.

Step 3: Formula (Pythagoras theorem): (OQ)^2 = (OP)^2 + (PQ)^2 = (sqrt(2))^2 + (1)^2 = 2 + 1 = 3, so OQ = sqrt(3).

Step 4: With O as centre and radius OQ = sqrt(3), draw an arc meeting the number line at R. Then OR = sqrt(3), so R represents sqrt(3).

(iii) 4 1/3: Step 1: 4 1/3 lies between 4 and 5.

Step 2: Divide the unit segment from 4 to 5 into 3 equal parts with points A and B.

Step 3: The first division point after 4 is 4 + 1/3 = 4 1/3. Mark it as P.

(iv) -2 1/7: Step 1: -2 1/7 lies between -2 and -3 on the left of 0.

Step 2: Divide the unit segment from -2 to -3 into 7 equal parts.

Step 3: The first division point on moving from -2 towards -3 is -2 - 1/7 = -2 1/7. Mark it as P.

(v) 5/8: Step 1: 5/8 lies between 0 and 1.

Step 2: Divide the unit segment from 0 to 1 into 8 equal parts.

Step 3: Count 5 parts from 0; the 5th division point is 5/8. Mark it as P.

(vi) 2 3/4: Step 1: 2 3/4 lies between 2 and 3.

Step 2: Divide the unit segment from 2 to 3 into 4 equal parts.

Step 3: Count 3 parts from 2; the 3rd division point is 2 + 3/4 = 2 3/4. Mark it as P.

Q3: Express the following as a rational number p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not 0

(i) 0.4 (bar on 4) (ii) 0.37 (bar on 37) (iii) 0.21 (bar on 21)

(i) Let x = 0.444...

Step 1: x = 0.444... ...(i)

Step 2: Multiply both sides by 10: 10x = 4.444... ...(ii)

Step 3: Subtract (i) from (ii): 10x - x = 4.444... - 0.444...

Step 4: 9x = 4

Step 5: x = 4/9. Hence 0.4 (bar) = 4/9.

(ii) Let x = 0.373737...

Step 1: x = 0.373737... ...(i)

Step 2: Multiply both sides by 100 (two digits repeat): 100x = 37.373737... ...(ii)

Step 3: Subtract (i) from (ii): 100x - x = 37.373737... - 0.373737...

Step 4: 99x = 37

Step 5: x = 37/99. Hence 0.37 (bar) = 37/99.

(iii) Let x = 0.212121...

Step 1: x = 0.212121... ...(i)

Step 2: Multiply both sides by 100: 100x = 21.212121... ...(ii)

Step 3: Subtract (i) from (ii): 100x - x = 21.212121... - 0.212121...

Step 4: 99x = 21

Step 5: x = 21/99 = 7/33 (dividing numerator and denominator by 3). Hence 0.21 (bar) = 7/33.

Q4: Name the property used in the following

(i) (a + 4) + b = a + (4 + b) (ii) sqrt(2) + sqrt(3) = sqrt(3) + sqrt(2) (iii) x - x = 0 (iv) a(b + c) = ab + ac (v) 16 + 0 = 16 (vi) 100 x 1 = 100 (vii) 4 x (5 x 8) = (4 x 5) x 8 (viii) ab = ba

(i) Associative property of addition (grouping changes, sum stays the same).

(ii) Commutative property of addition (order changes, sum stays the same).

(iii) Additive inverse property (a number minus itself gives 0).

(iv) Left distributive property of multiplication over addition.

(v) Additive identity property (0 is the additive identity).

(vi) Multiplicative identity property (1 is the multiplicative identity).

(vii) Associative property of multiplication.

(viii) Commutative property of multiplication.

Q5: Name the property used in the following

(i) -3 < -1 implies 0 < 2 (ii) If a < b then 1/a > 1/b (iii) If a < b then a + c < b + c (iv) If ac < bc and c > 0 then a < b (v) If ac < bc and c < 0 then a > b (vi) Either a > b or a = b or a < b

(i) Order (additive) property of inequality with respect to addition: 3 is added to both sides, -3 + 3 = 0 and -1 + 3 = 2, and the inequality sign stays the same.

(ii) Reciprocal property of inequality (for numbers of the same sign, taking reciprocals reverses the inequality).

(iii) Order (additive) property of inequality with respect to addition: adding the same number c to both sides keeps the inequality unchanged.

(iv) Multiplicative (cancellation) property of inequality: dividing both sides by the positive number c keeps the inequality unchanged.

(v) Multiplicative property of inequality: dividing both sides by the negative number c reverses the inequality.

(vi) Trichotomy property of real numbers.

Q6: Find two rational numbers between

(i) 1/3 and 1/4 (ii) 3 and 4 (iii) 3/5 and 4/5

Method: Formula: mean of two numbers = (first number + second number) / 2. The mean always lies between the two numbers.

(i) Between 1/3 and 1/4:

Step 1: First number = (1/3 + 1/4) / 2 = (7/12) / 2 = 7/24.

Step 2: Second number = mean of 7/24 and 1/3 = (7/24 + 8/24) / 2 = (15/24) / 2 = 15/48 = 5/16.

Hence two rational numbers between 1/4 and 1/3 are 7/24 and 5/16.

(ii) Between 3 and 4:

Step 1: First number = (3 + 4) / 2 = 7/2.

Step 2: Second number = mean of 7/2 and 4 = (7/2 + 4) / 2 = (15/2) / 2 = 15/4.

Hence two rational numbers between 3 and 4 are 7/2 and 15/4.

(iii) Between 3/5 and 4/5:

Step 1: First number = (3/5 + 4/5) / 2 = (7/5) / 2 = 7/10.

Step 2: Second number = mean of 7/10 and 4/5 = (7/10 + 8/10) / 2 = (15/10) / 2 = 15/20 = 3/4.

Hence two rational numbers between 3/5 and 4/5 are 7/10 and 3/4.

mcqs.q: The number 0.666... (6 recurring) is:
mcqs.why: A non-terminating recurring decimal can always be written in the form p/q. Here 0.666... = 6/9 = 2/3, so it is a rational number.

mcqs.q: sqrt(7) is an irrational number because:
options: 7 is a prime number greater than 5
7 is not a perfect square, so sqrt(7) is non-terminating and non-recurring
mcqs.why: Rule: if n is not a perfect square, sqrt(n) cannot be written in p/q form. Its decimal neither terminates nor recurs, so sqrt(7) is irrational.

mcqs.q: (2 - sqrt(2))(2 + sqrt(2)) is equal to:
mcqs.why: Formula: (a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2. Step 1: = (2)^2 - (sqrt(2))^2. Step 2: = 4 - 2. Step 3: = 2, which is rational (2/1).

mcqs.q: The recurring decimal 0.373737... (bar on 37) in p/q form is:
The recurring decimal 0.212121... (bar on 21) in its lowest p/q form is:
mcqs.why: Let x = 0.212121... Step 1: 100x - x = 21, so 99x = 21. Step 2: x = 21/99. Step 3: divide numerator and denominator by 3: x = 7/33.

mcqs.q: The property used in (a + 4) + b = a + (4 + b) is:
mcqs.why: Only the grouping (brackets) changes while the order of the numbers stays the same, and the sum is unchanged. That is the associative property of addition.

mcqs.q: The property used in a(b + c) = ab + ac is:
options: distributive property of multiplication over addition
mcqs.why: The factor a is distributed over the sum (b + c), giving ab + ac. Multiplication distributing over addition is the distributive property.

mcqs.q: The statement 16 + 0 = 16 shows the:
mcqs.why: Adding 0 leaves a number unchanged, so 0 is the additive identity. The additive inverse property would need 16 + (-16) = 0.

mcqs.q: Using the mean method, two rational numbers between 3 and 4 are:
mcqs.why: Formula: mean = (first + second)/2. Step 1: (3 + 4)/2 = 7/2. Step 2: mean of 7/2 and 4 = (7/2 + 4)/2 = (15/2)/2 = 15/4. Both lie between 3 and 4.

mcqs.q: On the number line, sqrt(3) is located after sqrt(2) by using a right triangle in which (OQ)^2 equals:
mcqs.why: Formula (Pythagoras theorem): (OQ)^2 = (OP)^2 + (PQ)^2 where OP = sqrt(2) and PQ = 1. Step: (OQ)^2 = (sqrt(2))^2 + (1)^2 = 2 + 1 = 3, so OQ = sqrt(3).

lessons.title: Exercise 1.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1: Rationalize the denominator of the following

(i) 13 / (4 + sqrt(3)) (ii) (sqrt(2) + sqrt(5)) / sqrt(3) (iii) (sqrt(2) - 1) / sqrt(5) (iv) (6 - 4 sqrt(2)) / (6 + 4 sqrt(2)) (v) (sqrt(3) - sqrt(2)) / (sqrt(3) + sqrt(2)) (vi) 4 sqrt(3) / (sqrt(7) + sqrt(5))

Method: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. Formula: (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2.

(i) 13 / (4 + sqrt(3)): conjugate of 4 + sqrt(3) is 4 - sqrt(3).

Step 1: = [13 x (4 - sqrt(3))] / [(4 + sqrt(3))(4 - sqrt(3))]

Step 2: Denominator = (4)^2 - (sqrt(3))^2 = 16 - 3 = 13.

Step 3: = 13(4 - sqrt(3)) / 13 = 4 - sqrt(3).

(ii) (sqrt(2) + sqrt(5)) / sqrt(3): multiply numerator and denominator by sqrt(3).

Step 1: = [(sqrt(2) + sqrt(5)) x sqrt(3)] / (sqrt(3) x sqrt(3))

Step 2: = (sqrt(6) + sqrt(15)) / 3 [Formula: sqrt(a) x sqrt(b) = sqrt(ab)]

(iii) (sqrt(2) - 1) / sqrt(5): multiply numerator and denominator by sqrt(5).

Step 1: = [(sqrt(2) - 1) x sqrt(5)] / (sqrt(5) x sqrt(5))

Step 2: = (sqrt(10) - sqrt(5)) / 5.

(iv) (6 - 4 sqrt(2)) / (6 + 4 sqrt(2)): conjugate of 6 + 4 sqrt(2) is 6 - 4 sqrt(2).

Step 1: = (6 - 4 sqrt(2))^2 / [(6 + 4 sqrt(2))(6 - 4 sqrt(2))]

Step 2: Numerator: Formula: (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2, so (6 - 4 sqrt(2))^2 = 36 - 48 sqrt(2) + 16 x 2 = 36 - 48 sqrt(2) + 32 = 68 - 48 sqrt(2).

Step 3: Denominator = (6)^2 - (4 sqrt(2))^2 = 36 - 32 = 4.

Step 4: = (68 - 48 sqrt(2)) / 4 = 17 - 12 sqrt(2).

(v) (sqrt(3) - sqrt(2)) / (sqrt(3) + sqrt(2)): conjugate of sqrt(3) + sqrt(2) is sqrt(3) - sqrt(2).

Step 1: = (sqrt(3) - sqrt(2))^2 / [(sqrt(3) + sqrt(2))(sqrt(3) - sqrt(2))]

Step 2: Numerator = 3 - 2 sqrt(6) + 2 = 5 - 2 sqrt(6).

Step 3: Denominator = (sqrt(3))^2 - (sqrt(2))^2 = 3 - 2 = 1.

Step 4: = 5 - 2 sqrt(6).

(vi) 4 sqrt(3) / (sqrt(7) + sqrt(5)): conjugate of sqrt(7) + sqrt(5) is sqrt(7) - sqrt(5).

Step 1: = [4 sqrt(3) x (sqrt(7) - sqrt(5))] / [(sqrt(7) + sqrt(5))(sqrt(7) - sqrt(5))]

Step 2: Denominator = 7 - 5 = 2.

Step 3: = 4 (sqrt(21) - sqrt(15)) / 2 = 2 sqrt(21) - 2 sqrt(15).

Q2: Simplify the following

(i) (81/16)^(-3/4) (ii) (3/4)^(-2) / (4/9)^3 x 16/27 (iii) (0.027)^(-1/3) (iv) 7th root of [x^14 y^21 z^35 / (y^14 z^7)] (v) [5.(25)^(n+1) - 25.(5)^(2n)] / [5.(5)^(2n+3) - (25)^(n+1)] (vi) [(16)^(x+1) + 20(4)^(2x)] / [2^(x-3) x 8^(x+2)] (vii) (64)^(-2/3) / (9)^(-3/2) (viii) [3^n x 9^(n+1)] / [3^(n-1) x 9^(n-1)] (ix) [5^(n+3) - 6.5^(n+1)] / [9 x 5^n - 4 x 5^n]

Laws used: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n); a^m / a^n = a^(m-n); (a^m)^n = a^(mn); a^(-m) = 1/a^m; nth root of a = a^(1/n).

(i) (81/16)^(-3/4): Step 1: 81/16 = (3/2)^4, so = [(3/2)^4]^(-3/4).

Step 2: Formula: (a^m)^n = a^(mn), so = (3/2)^(4 x -3/4) = (3/2)^(-3).

Step 3: = (2/3)^3 = 8/27.

(ii) Step 1: (3/4)^(-2) = (4/3)^2 = 16/9.

Step 2: (4/9)^3 = 64/729.

Step 3: (16/9) / (64/729) = (16/9) x (729/64) = (16 x 81) / 64 = 81/4.

Step 4: (81/4) x (16/27) = 3 x 4 = 12.

(iii) (0.027)^(-1/3): Step 1: 0.027 = 27/1000 = (3/10)^3.

Step 2: = [(3/10)^3]^(-1/3) = (3/10)^(-1) = 10/3.

(iv) Step 1: Inside the root, divide powers of the same base: x^14 y^(21-14) z^(35-7) = x^14 y^7 z^28.

Step 2: 7th root = (x^14 y^7 z^28)^(1/7) = x^(14/7) y^(7/7) z^(28/7) = x^2 y z^4.

(v) Step 1: Write 25 = 5^2. Numerator = 5 x 5^(2n+2) - 5^2 x 5^(2n) = 5^(2n+3) - 5^(2n+2).

Step 2: Take 5^(2n+2) common: Numerator = 5^(2n+2) (5 - 1) = 4 x 5^(2n+2).

Step 3: Denominator = 5 x 5^(2n+3) - 5^(2n+2) = 5^(2n+4) - 5^(2n+2) = 5^(2n+2) (25 - 1) = 24 x 5^(2n+2).

Step 4: Ratio = 4 / 24 = 1/6.

(vi) Step 1: Numerator: (16)^(x+1) = 16 x 16^x = 16 x 4^(2x), so Numerator = 4^(2x) (16 + 20) = 36 x 4^(2x).

Step 2: Denominator = 2^(x-3) x 2^(3x+6) = 2^(4x+3) = 8 x 2^(4x) = 8 x 4^(2x).

Step 3: Ratio = 36 / 8 = 9/2.

(vii) Step 1: (64)^(-2/3) = 1 / (64)^(2/3) = 1 / (4^3)^(2/3) = 1 / 4^2 = 1/16.

Step 2: (9)^(-3/2) = 1 / (9)^(3/2) = 1 / (3^2)^(3/2) = 1 / 3^3 = 1/27.

Step 3: (1/16) / (1/27) = 27/16.

(viii) Step 1: Write 9 = 3^2. Numerator = 3^n x 3^(2n+2) = 3^(3n+2).

Step 2: Denominator = 3^(n-1) x 3^(2n-2) = 3^(3n-3).

Step 3: Ratio = 3^[(3n+2) - (3n-3)] = 3^5 = 243.

(ix) Step 1: Numerator = 5^(n+1) (5^2 - 6) = 5^(n+1) (25 - 6) = 19 x 5^(n+1).

Step 2: Denominator = 5^n (9 - 4) = 5 x 5^n = 5^(n+1).

Step 3: Ratio = 19.

Q3: If x = 3 + sqrt(8), then find the value of

(i) x + 1/x (ii) x - 1/x (iii) x^2 + 1/x^2 (iv) x^2 - 1/x^2 (v) x^4 + 1/x^4 (vi) (x - 1/x)^2

Given x = 3 + sqrt(8) = 3 + 2 sqrt(2).

Step 1: Find 1/x by rationalizing: 1/x = 1 / (3 + 2 sqrt(2)) = (3 - 2 sqrt(2)) / [(3)^2 - (2 sqrt(2))^2] = (3 - 2 sqrt(2)) / (9 - 8) = 3 - 2 sqrt(2).

(i) x + 1/x = (3 + 2 sqrt(2)) + (3 - 2 sqrt(2)) = 6.

(ii) x - 1/x = (3 + 2 sqrt(2)) - (3 - 2 sqrt(2)) = 4 sqrt(2).

(iii) Formula: x^2 + 1/x^2 = (x + 1/x)^2 - 2.

Step: = (6)^2 - 2 = 36 - 2 = 34.

(iv) Formula: x^2 - 1/x^2 = (x - 1/x)(x + 1/x).

Step: = (4 sqrt(2))(6) = 24 sqrt(2).

(v) Formula: x^4 + 1/x^4 = (x^2 + 1/x^2)^2 - 2.

Step: = (34)^2 - 2 = 1156 - 2 = 1154.

(vi) (x - 1/x)^2 = (4 sqrt(2))^2 = 16 x 2 = 32.

Q4: Find the rational numbers p and q such that (8 - 3 sqrt(2)) / (4 + 3 sqrt(2)) = p + q sqrt(2)

Find p and q.

Step 1: Rationalize the left side by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate 4 - 3 sqrt(2).

Step 2: Numerator = (8 - 3 sqrt(2))(4 - 3 sqrt(2)) = 32 - 24 sqrt(2) - 12 sqrt(2) + 9 x 2 = 32 - 36 sqrt(2) + 18 = 50 - 36 sqrt(2).

Step 3: Denominator = (4)^2 - (3 sqrt(2))^2 = 16 - 18 = -2.

Step 4: LHS = (50 - 36 sqrt(2)) / (-2) = -25 + 18 sqrt(2).

Step 5: Compare with p + q sqrt(2): p = -25 and q = 18.

Q5: Simplify the following

(i) [(25)^(3/2) x (243)^(3/5)] / [(16)^(5/4) x (8)^(4/3)] (ii) [54 x cube root of (27)^(2x)] / [9^(x+1) + 216(3)^(2x-1)] (iii) sqrt{ [(216)^(2/3) x (25)^(1/2)] / (0.04)^(-3/2) } (iv) (a^(1/3) + b^(2/3)) x (a^(2/3) - a^(1/3) b^(2/3) + b^(4/3))

(i) Step 1: (25)^(3/2) = (5^2)^(3/2) = 5^3 = 125.

Step 2: (243)^(3/5) = (3^5)^(3/5) = 3^3 = 27.

Step 3: Numerator = 125 x 27 = 3375.

Step 4: (16)^(5/4) = (2^4)^(5/4) = 2^5 = 32; (8)^(4/3) = (2^3)^(4/3) = 2^4 = 16. Denominator = 32 x 16 = 512.

Step 5: Result = 3375 / 512.

(ii) Step 1: Cube root of (27)^(2x) = [(27)^(2x)]^(1/3) = 27^(2x/3) = (3^3)^(2x/3) = 3^(2x). Numerator = 54 x 3^(2x).

Step 2: Denominator: 9^(x+1) = 3^(2x+2) = 9 x 3^(2x); 216 x 3^(2x-1) = (216/3) x 3^(2x) = 72 x 3^(2x). Denominator = (9 + 72) x 3^(2x) = 81 x 3^(2x).

Step 3: Ratio = 54 / 81 = 2/3.

(iii) Step 1: (216)^(2/3) = (6^3)^(2/3) = 6^2 = 36; (25)^(1/2) = 5. Numerator inside = 36 x 5 = 180.

Step 2: (0.04)^(-3/2) = (1/25)^(-3/2) = 25^(3/2) = (5^2)^(3/2) = 5^3 = 125.

Step 3: Inside the square root = 180 / 125 = 36/25.

Step 4: Square root = sqrt(36) / sqrt(25) = 6/5.

(iv) Step 1: Put X = a^(1/3) and Y = b^(2/3). Then the second factor is X^2 - XY + Y^2.

Step 2: Formula: (X + Y)(X^2 - XY + Y^2) = X^3 + Y^3.

Step 3: X^3 = [a^(1/3)]^3 = a; Y^3 = [b^(2/3)]^3 = b^2.

Step 4: Result = a + b^2.

mcqs.q: After rationalizing the denominator, 13 / (4 + sqrt(3)) becomes:
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate 4 - sqrt(3). Denominator = (4)^2 - (sqrt(3))^2 = 16 - 3 = 13. So the fraction = 13(4 - sqrt(3))/13 = 4 - sqrt(3).

mcqs.q: If x = 3 + sqrt(8), then x + 1/x is equal to:
If x = 3 + sqrt(8), then x^2 + 1/x^2 is equal to:
(6 - 4 sqrt(2)) / (6 + 4 sqrt(2)) simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate 6 - 4 sqrt(2). Step 2: Numerator = 36 - 48 sqrt(2) + 32 = 68 - 48 sqrt(2). Step 3: Denominator = 36 - 32 = 4. Step 4: = (68 - 48 sqrt(2))/4 = 17 - 12 sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: (sqrt(3) - sqrt(2)) / (sqrt(3) + sqrt(2)) simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate sqrt(3) - sqrt(2). Step 2: Numerator = (sqrt(3) - sqrt(2))^2 = 3 - 2 sqrt(6) + 2 = 5 - 2 sqrt(6). Step 3: Denominator = 3 - 2 = 1. Result = 5 - 2 sqrt(6).

mcqs.q: If (8 - 3 sqrt(2)) / (4 + 3 sqrt(2)) = p + q sqrt(2), then p and q are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Rationalize with the conjugate 4 - 3 sqrt(2): numerator = 50 - 36 sqrt(2), denominator = 16 - 18 = -2. Step 2: LHS = -25 + 18 sqrt(2). Step 3: Comparing, p = -25 and q = 18.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1

The sum of three consecutive integers is forty-two. Find the three integers.

Step 1: Let the three consecutive integers be n, n + 1 and n + 2.

Step 2: Sum = n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 42.

Step 3: 3n + 3 = 42.

Step 4: 3n = 42 - 3 = 39.

Step 5: n = 39 / 3 = 13.

Hence the three integers are 13, 14 and 15. (Check: 13 + 14 + 15 = 42.)

Q2

The diagram shows right-angled triangle ABC in which the length of AC is (sqrt(3) + sqrt(5)) cm. The area of triangle ABC is (1 + sqrt(15)) cm^2. Find the length AB in the form (a sqrt(3) + b sqrt(5)) cm, where a and b are integers. [Diagram: right angle at A; base AC labelled (sqrt(3)+sqrt(5)) cm; B above A.]

Step 1: Formula: Area of a triangle = (1/2) x base x height. Here base = AC and height = AB, so Area = (1/2) x AB x AC.

Step 2: AB = (2 x Area) / AC = [2(1 + sqrt(15))] / (sqrt(3) + sqrt(5)).

Step 3: Rationalize by multiplying numerator and denominator by (sqrt(5) - sqrt(3)): Denominator = (sqrt(5))^2 - (sqrt(3))^2 = 5 - 3 = 2.

Step 4: Numerator = 2(1 + sqrt(15))(sqrt(5) - sqrt(3)) = 2[sqrt(5) - sqrt(3) + sqrt(75) - sqrt(45)].

Step 5: sqrt(75) = 5 sqrt(3) and sqrt(45) = 3 sqrt(5), so Numerator = 2[sqrt(5) - sqrt(3) + 5 sqrt(3) - 3 sqrt(5)] = 2[4 sqrt(3) - 2 sqrt(5)] = 8 sqrt(3) - 4 sqrt(5).

Step 6: AB = (8 sqrt(3) - 4 sqrt(5)) / 2 = 4 sqrt(3) - 2 sqrt(5) cm. Hence a = 4 and b = -2.

Q3

A rectangle has sides of length (2 + sqrt(18)) m and (5 - 4/sqrt(2)) m. Express the area of the rectangle in the form a + b sqrt(2), where a and b are integers.

Step 1: Simplify the sides: sqrt(18) = sqrt(9 x 2) = 3 sqrt(2), so first side = 2 + 3 sqrt(2).

Step 2: 4 / sqrt(2) = (4 sqrt(2)) / 2 = 2 sqrt(2), so second side = 5 - 2 sqrt(2).

Step 3: Formula: Area of rectangle = length x breadth.

Step 4: Area = (2 + 3 sqrt(2))(5 - 2 sqrt(2)) = 10 - 4 sqrt(2) + 15 sqrt(2) - 6 x (sqrt(2))^2.

Step 5: = 10 + 11 sqrt(2) - 6 x 2 = 10 + 11 sqrt(2) - 12 = -2 + 11 sqrt(2).

Hence Area = (-2 + 11 sqrt(2)) m^2, so a = -2 and b = 11.

Q4

Find two numbers whose sum is 68 and difference is 22.

Step 1: Let the numbers be x and y. Then x + y = 68 ...(i) and x - y = 22 ...(ii).

Step 2: Add (i) and (ii): 2x = 90, so x = 45.

Step 3: Put x = 45 in (i): 45 + y = 68, so y = 68 - 45 = 23.

Hence the two numbers are 45 and 23. (Check: 45 + 23 = 68; 45 - 23 = 22.)

Q5

The weather in Lahore was unusually warm during the summer of 2024. The TV news reported temperature as high as 48 degrees C. By using the formula F = (9/5) C + 32, find the temperature on the Fahrenheit scale.

Step 1: Formula: F = (9/5) x C + 32, where C = 48.

Step 2: Substitute C = 48: F = (9/5) x 48 + 32.

Step 3: (9/5) x 48 = 432 / 5 = 86.4.

Step 4: F = 86.4 + 32 = 118.4.

Hence the temperature is 118.4 degrees F.

Q6

The sum of the ages of the father and son is 72 years. Six years ago, the father's age was 2 times the age of the son. What was the son's age six years ago?

Step 1: Let the son's present age be s years. Then the father's present age = 72 - s years.

Step 2: Six years ago: son's age = s - 6; father's age = 72 - s - 6 = 66 - s.

Step 3: Given condition: 66 - s = 2(s - 6).

Step 4: 66 - s = 2s - 12.

Step 5: 66 + 12 = 2s + s, so 78 = 3s.

Step 6: s = 78 / 3 = 26 years (son's present age).

Step 7: Son's age six years ago = 26 - 6 = 20 years.

Q7

Mirha bought a toy for Rs. 1500 and sold it for Rs. 1520. What was her profit percentage?

Step 1: Cost Price = CP = Rs. 1500; Selling Price = SP = Rs. 1520.

Step 2: Formula: Profit = SP - CP = 1520 - 1500 = Rs. 20.

Step 3: Formula: Profit % = (Profit / CP) x 100.

Step 4: Profit % = (20 / 1500) x 100 = 2000 / 1500 = 1.33%.

Hence her profit percentage is 1.33%.

Q8

The annual income of Tayyab is Rs. 9,60,000, while the exempted amount is Rs. 1,30,000. How much tax would he have to pay at the rate of 0.75%?

Step 1: Taxable income = Annual income - Exempted amount.

Step 2: Taxable income = 9,60,000 - 1,30,000 = Rs. 8,30,000.

Step 3: Formula: Tax = Taxable income x (Rate / 100).

Step 4: Tax = 8,30,000 x (0.75 / 100) = 8,30,000 x 0.0075 = Rs. 6,225.

Hence Tayyab has to pay a tax of Rs. 6,225.

Q9

Find the compound markup on Rs. 3,75,000 for one year at the rate of 14% compounded annually.

Step 1: Principal P = Rs. 3,75,000; Rate R = 14%; Time n = 1 year.

Step 2: Formula: Amount A = P (1 + R/100)^n.

Step 3: A = 3,75,000 x (1 + 14/100)^1 = 3,75,000 x 1.14.

Step 4: A = Rs. 4,27,500.

Step 5: Formula: Compound markup = A - P = 4,27,500 - 3,75,000 = Rs. 52,500.

Hence the compound markup is Rs. 52,500.

mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the integers be n, n + 1, n + 2. Step 2: n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 42, so 3n + 3 = 42. Step 3: 3n = 39, n = 13. The integers are 13, 14 and 15.

In right-angled triangle ABC (right angle at A), AC = (sqrt(3) + sqrt(5)) cm and the area is (1 + sqrt(15)) cm^2. The length AB is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Formula: Area = (1/2) x AB x AC, so AB = 2(1 + sqrt(15))/(sqrt(3) + sqrt(5)). Step 2: Rationalize with (sqrt(5) - sqrt(3)): denominator = 5 - 3 = 2. Step 3: Numerator = 2[sqrt(5) - sqrt(3) + 5 sqrt(3) - 3 sqrt(5)] = 8 sqrt(3) - 4 sqrt(5). Step 4: AB = (8 sqrt(3) - 4 sqrt(5))/2 = 4 sqrt(3) - 2 sqrt(5) cm.

mcqs.q: A rectangle has sides (2 + sqrt(18)) m and (5 - 4/sqrt(2)) m. Its area in the form a + b sqrt(2) is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: sqrt(18) = 3 sqrt(2), so one side = 2 + 3 sqrt(2); 4/sqrt(2) = 2 sqrt(2), so the other side = 5 - 2 sqrt(2). Step 2: Formula: Area = length x breadth = (2 + 3 sqrt(2))(5 - 2 sqrt(2)) = 10 + 11 sqrt(2) - 12 = -2 + 11 sqrt(2) m^2.

mcqs.q: To solve 'the sum of three consecutive integers is 42', the integers are first taken as:
options: n - 1, n and n + 1 only for even sums
mcqs.why: Consecutive integers differ by 1, so if the first is n the next two are n + 1 and n + 2. Their sum gives 3n + 3 = 42, hence n = 13.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
Q1 (i)

sqrt(7) is:
(a) integer   (b) rational number   (c) irrational number   (d) natural number
Correct answer: irrational number

Q1 (ii)

pi and e are:
(a) natural numbers   (b) integers   (c) rational numbers   (d) irrational numbers
Correct answer: irrational numbers

Q1 (iii)

If n is not a perfect square, then sqrt(n) is:
(a) rational number   (b) natural number   (c) integer   (d) irrational number
Correct answer: irrational number

Q1 (iv)

sqrt(3) + sqrt(5) is:
(a) whole number   (b) integer   (c) rational number   (d) irrational number
Correct answer: irrational number

Q1 (v)

For all x in R, x = x is called:
(a) reflexive property   (b) transitive property   (c) symmetric property   (d) trichotomy property
Correct answer: reflexive property

Q1 (vi)

Let a, b, c in R, then a > b and b > c implies a > c is called ______ property.
(a) trichotomy   (b) transitive   (c) additive   (d) multiplicative
Correct answer: transitive

Q1 (vii)

2^x x 8^x = 64 then x =
(a) 3/2   (b) 3/4   (c) 5/6   (d) 2/3
Correct answer: 3/2

Q1 (viii)

Let a, b in R, then a = b and b = a is called ______ property.
(a) reflexive   (b) symmetric   (c) transitive   (d) additive
Correct answer: symmetric

Q1 (ix)

sqrt(75) + sqrt(27) =
(a) sqrt(102)   (b) 9 sqrt(3)   (c) 5 sqrt(3)   (d) 8 sqrt(3)
Correct answer: 8 sqrt(3)

Q1 (x)

The product of (3 + sqrt(5))(3 - sqrt(5)) is:
(a) prime number   (b) odd number   (c) irrational number   (d) rational number
Correct answer: rational number

Q2: If a = 3/2, b = 5/3 and c = 7/5, then verify that

(i) a(b + c) = ab + ac (ii) (a + b)c = ac + bc

(i) Left distributive property: Formula: a(b + c) = ab + ac.

Step 1: b + c = 5/3 + 7/5 = (25 + 21) / 15 = 46/15.

Step 2: LHS = a(b + c) = (3/2) x (46/15) = 138/30 = 23/5.

Step 3: ab = (3/2)(5/3) = 5/2; ac = (3/2)(7/5) = 21/10.

Step 4: RHS = ab + ac = 5/2 + 21/10 = (25 + 21) / 10 = 46/10 = 23/5.

Step 5: LHS = RHS = 23/5. Verified.

(ii) Right distributive property: Formula: (a + b)c = ac + bc.

Step 1: a + b = 3/2 + 5/3 = (9 + 10) / 6 = 19/6.

Step 2: LHS = (a + b)c = (19/6)(7/5) = 133/30.

Step 3: ac = (3/2)(7/5) = 21/10 = 63/30; bc = (5/3)(7/5) = 7/3 = 70/30.

Step 4: RHS = ac + bc = 63/30 + 70/30 = 133/30.

Step 5: LHS = RHS = 133/30. Verified.

Q3: If a = 4/3, b = 5/2, c = 7/4, then verify the associative property of real numbers w.r.t. addition and multiplication

Verify: (i) (a + b) + c = a + (b + c) (ii) (ab)c = a(bc)

(i) Addition: Formula: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c).

Step 1: a + b = 4/3 + 5/2 = (8 + 15) / 6 = 23/6.

Step 2: LHS = (a + b) + c = 23/6 + 7/4 = (46 + 21) / 12 = 67/12.

Step 3: b + c = 5/2 + 7/4 = (10 + 7) / 4 = 17/4.

Step 4: RHS = a + (b + c) = 4/3 + 17/4 = (16 + 51) / 12 = 67/12.

Step 5: LHS = RHS. Associative property of addition is verified.

(ii) Multiplication: Formula: (ab)c = a(bc).

Step 1: ab = (4/3)(5/2) = 20/6 = 10/3.

Step 2: LHS = (ab)c = (10/3)(7/4) = 70/12 = 35/6.

Step 3: bc = (5/2)(7/4) = 35/8.

Step 4: RHS = a(bc) = (4/3)(35/8) = 140/24 = 35/6.

Step 5: LHS = RHS. Associative property of multiplication is verified.

Q4

Is 0 a rational number? Explain.

Yes, 0 is a rational number.

Step 1: A rational number is a number that can be written in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not 0.

Step 2: 0 can be written as 0/1, where p = 0 and q = 1 (not 0).

Step 3: Hence 0 satisfies the definition, so 0 is a rational number.

Q5

State the trichotomy property of real numbers.

Trichotomy property: For any two real numbers a and b, exactly one of the following three relations holds:

a > b, or a = b, or a < b.

That is, two real numbers can always be compared, and only one of the three cases is true at a time.

Q6

Find two rational numbers between 4 and 5.

Method: Formula: mean = (first number + second number) / 2.

Step 1: First number = (4 + 5) / 2 = 9/2.

Step 2: Second number = mean of 9/2 and 5 = (9/2 + 5) / 2 = (19/2) / 2 = 19/4.

Hence two rational numbers between 4 and 5 are 9/2 and 19/4.

Q7: Simplify the following

(i) 5th root of (x^15 y^35 / z^20) (ii) cube root of (27)^(2x) (iii) 6(3)^(n+2) / (3^(n+1) - 3^n)

(i) Step 1: 5th root means power 1/5: = (x^15 y^35 z^(-20))^(1/5).

Step 2: Formula: (a^m)^(1/n) = a^(m/n), so = x^(15/5) y^(35/5) z^(-20/5) = x^3 y^7 / z^4.

(ii) Step 1: Cube root of (27)^(2x) = [(27)^(2x)]^(1/3) = 27^(2x/3).

Step 2: 27 = 3^3, so = (3^3)^(2x/3) = 3^(2x) = 9^x.

(iii) Step 1: Numerator = 6 x 3^(n+2) = 6 x 9 x 3^n = 54 x 3^n.

Step 2: Denominator = 3^n (3 - 1) = 2 x 3^n [taking 3^n common: 3^(n+1) = 3 x 3^n].

Step 3: Ratio = 54 / 2 = 27.

Q8

The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 51. Find the three integers.

Step 1: Let the three consecutive odd integers be n, n + 2 and n + 4.

Step 2: Sum = n + (n + 2) + (n + 4) = 51.

Step 3: 3n + 6 = 51.

Step 4: 3n = 51 - 6 = 45.

Step 5: n = 45 / 3 = 15.

Hence the three odd integers are 15, 17 and 19. (Check: 15 + 17 + 19 = 51.)

Q9

Abdullah picked up 96 balls and placed them into two buckets. One bucket has twenty-eight more balls than the other bucket. How many balls were in each bucket?

Step 1: Let the smaller bucket contain x balls. Then the other bucket contains x + 28 balls.

Step 2: Total: x + (x + 28) = 96.

Step 3: 2x + 28 = 96.

Step 4: 2x = 96 - 28 = 68.

Step 5: x = 68 / 2 = 34.

Step 6: Other bucket = 34 + 28 = 62.

Hence the buckets contain 34 balls and 62 balls. (Check: 34 + 62 = 96.)

Q10

Salma invested Rs. 3,50,000 in a bank, which paid simple profit at the rate of 7 1/4 % per annum. After 2 years, the rate was increased to 8% per annum. Find the amount she had at the end of 7 years.

Step 1: Principal P = Rs. 3,50,000. Formula: Simple profit = (P x R x T) / 100.

Step 2: Profit for the first 2 years at 7 1/4 % = 29/4 %: = (3,50,000 x 29/4 x 2) / 100 = (3,50,000 x 58) / 400 = Rs. 50,750.

Step 3: Remaining time = 7 - 2 = 5 years at 8%: Profit = (3,50,000 x 8 x 5) / 100 = Rs. 1,40,000.

Step 4: Total profit = 50,750 + 1,40,000 = Rs. 1,90,750.

Step 5: Formula: Amount = Principal + Total profit = 3,50,000 + 1,90,750 = Rs. 5,40,750.

Hence Salma had Rs. 5,40,750 at the end of 7 years.

mcqs.q: sqrt(7) is:
mcqs.why: 7 is not a perfect square, so sqrt(7) is non-terminating and non-recurring; it cannot be written in p/q form, hence it is an irrational number.

mcqs.q: pi and e are:
mcqs.why: pi = 3.141592653589793... and e = 2.71828182845904... are both non-terminating and non-recurring decimals, so both are irrational numbers.

mcqs.q: If n is not a perfect square, then sqrt(n) is:
mcqs.why: The square root of a non-square natural number can never be expressed as p/q; its decimal expansion neither terminates nor recurs, so it is irrational.

mcqs.q: sqrt(3) + sqrt(5) is:
mcqs.why: Both sqrt(3) and sqrt(5) are irrational, and their sum does not terminate or recur, so sqrt(3) + sqrt(5) is an irrational number.

mcqs.q: For all x in R, x = x is called:
mcqs.why: Every real number is equal to itself: x = x. A quantity being equal to itself is the reflexive property of equality.

mcqs.q: Let a, b, c in R. Then a > b and b > c implies a > c is called the ______ property.
mcqs.why: The relation passes through the middle quantity b: a > b and b > c give a > c. This chaining is the transitive property.

Let a, b in R. Then a = b and b = a is called the ______ property.
mcqs.why: Equality can be read in either order: if a = b then b = a. Reversing the two sides is the symmetric property of equality.

mcqs.q: sqrt(75) + sqrt(27) =
mcqs.why: Step 1: sqrt(75) = sqrt(25 x 3) = 5 sqrt(3). Step 2: sqrt(27) = sqrt(9 x 3) = 3 sqrt(3). Step 3: Sum = 5 sqrt(3) + 3 sqrt(3) = 8 sqrt(3).

mcqs.q: The product of (3 + sqrt(5))(3 - sqrt(5)) is a:
mcqs.why: Formula: (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2. Step: (3)^2 - (sqrt(5))^2 = 9 - 5 = 4 = 4/1, which is in p/q form, so the product is a rational number.

mcqs.q: 0 is a rational number because:
options: 0 is an integer, and integers are not rational
0 can be written as 0/1, which is in p/q form with q not equal to 0
0 cannot be written as a fraction
mcqs.why: A rational number is any number writable as p/q with p, q integers and q not 0. Since 0 = 0/1 satisfies this, 0 is a rational number.

mcqs.q: Two rational numbers between 4 and 5, found by the mean method, are:
mcqs.why: Formula: mean = (first + second)/2. Step 1: (4 + 5)/2 = 9/2. Step 2: mean of 9/2 and 5 = (9/2 + 5)/2 = (19/2)/2 = 19/4. Both lie between 4 and 5.

mcqs.q: The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 51. The integers are:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the odd integers be n, n + 2, n + 4. Step 2: 3n + 6 = 51, so 3n = 45. Step 3: n = 15. The integers are 15, 17 and 19 (check: 15 + 17 + 19 = 51).

mcqs.q: 96 balls are placed into two buckets, one holding 28 more than the other. The buckets hold:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the smaller bucket hold x balls; the other holds x + 28. Step 2: x + (x + 28) = 96, so 2x = 68. Step 3: x = 34, and the other bucket = 34 + 28 = 62.

mcqs.q: 6(3)^(n+2) / (3^(n+1) - 3^n) simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Numerator = 6 x 3^(n+2) = 6 x 9 x 3^n = 54 x 3^n. Step 2: Denominator = 3^n (3 - 1) = 2 x 3^n, taking 3^n common. Step 3: Ratio = 54/2 = 27.

lessons.notes_html:
Q1: Express the following numbers in scientific notation

(i) 2000000 (ii) 48900 (iii) 0.0042 (iv) 0.0000009 (v) 73 x 10^3 (vi) 0.65 x 10^2

Rule: Scientific notation is a x 10^n, where 1 <= a < 10 and n is an integer. Move the decimal point until one non-zero digit is left of it; the count of places moved is n (positive when moved left, negative when moved right).

(i) 2000000: Step 1: Move the point 6 places left: 2. Step 2: = 2 x 10^6.

(ii) 48900: Step 1: Move the point 4 places left: 4.89. Step 2: = 4.89 x 10^4.

(iii) 0.0042: Step 1: Move the point 3 places right: 4.2. Step 2: = 4.2 x 10^(-3).

(iv) 0.0000009: Step 1: Move the point 7 places right: 9. Step 2: = 9 x 10^(-7).

(v) 73 x 10^3: Step 1: 73 = 7.3 x 10^1. Step 2: = 7.3 x 10^(1+3) = 7.3 x 10^4.

(vi) 0.65 x 10^2: Step 1: 0.65 = 6.5 x 10^(-1). Step 2: = 6.5 x 10^(-1+2) = 6.5 x 10^1.

Q2: Express the following numbers in ordinary notation

(i) 8.04 x 10^2 (ii) 3 x 10^5 (iii) 1.5 x 10^(-2) (iv) 1.77 x 10^7 (v) 5.5 x 10^(-6) (vi) 4 x 10^(-5)

Rule: For a positive exponent move the decimal point right; for a negative exponent move it left.

(i) 8.04 x 10^2: Move the point 2 places right: = 804.

(ii) 3 x 10^5: Move the point 5 places right: = 300,000.

(iii) 1.5 x 10^(-2): Move the point 2 places left: = 0.015.

(iv) 1.77 x 10^7: Move the point 7 places right: = 17,700,000.

(v) 5.5 x 10^(-6): Move the point 6 places left: = 0.0000055.

(vi) 4 x 10^(-5): Move the point 5 places left: = 0.00004.

Q3

The speed of light is approximately 3 x 10^8 metres per second. Express it in standard form.

Step 1: 3 x 10^8 means move the decimal point of 3 eight places to the right.

Step 2: 3 x 10^8 = 300,000,000.

Hence the speed of light is 300,000,000 metres per second in standard (ordinary) form.

Q4

The circumference of the Earth at the equator is about 40075000 metres. Express this number in scientific notation.

Step 1: Move the decimal point until one non-zero digit is left of it: 40075000 gives 4.0075.

Step 2: The point moved 7 places to the left, so the exponent is +7.

Step 3: 40075000 = 4.0075 x 10^7 metres.

Q5

The diameter of Mars is 6.779 x 10^3 km. Express this number in standard form.

Step 1: Positive exponent 3, so move the decimal point 3 places to the right.

Step 2: 6.779 x 10^3 = 6779.

Hence the diameter of Mars is 6779 km in standard form.

Q6

The diameter of Earth is about 1.2756 x 10^4 km. Express this number in standard form.

Step 1: Positive exponent 4, so move the decimal point 4 places to the right.

Step 2: 1.2756 x 10^4 = 12756.

Hence the diameter of Earth is 12,756 km in standard form.

mcqs.q: 48900 in scientific notation is:
mcqs.why: Rule: scientific notation is a x 10^n with 1 <= a < 10. Move the decimal point 4 places left to get 4.89, so 48900 = 4.89 x 10^4.

mcqs.q: 0.0042 in scientific notation is:
mcqs.why: Move the decimal point 3 places right to get 4.2. Moving right gives a negative exponent, so 0.0042 = 4.2 x 10^(-3).

mcqs.q: 73 x 10^3 in proper scientific notation is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: 73 = 7.3 x 10^1. Step 2: 7.3 x 10^1 x 10^3 = 7.3 x 10^(1+3) = 7.3 x 10^4, because the first factor must lie between 1 and 10.

mcqs.q: 8.04 x 10^2 in ordinary notation is:
mcqs.why: A positive exponent 2 means move the decimal point 2 places to the right: 8.04 becomes 804.

mcqs.q: 1.5 x 10^(-2) in ordinary notation is:
mcqs.why: A negative exponent -2 means move the decimal point 2 places to the left: 1.5 becomes 0.015.

mcqs.q: The speed of light, 3 x 10^8 m/s, in standard form is:

mcqs.q: In scientific notation a x 10^n, the value of a must satisfy:
mcqs.why: By definition, scientific notation writes a number as a x 10^n where the coefficient a has exactly one non-zero digit before the decimal point, i.e. 1 <= a < 10, and n is an integer.

mcqs.q: 5.5 x 10^(-6) in ordinary notation is:

lessons.title: Exercise 2.2
lessons.notes_html:
Q1: Express each of the following in logarithmic form

(i) 10^3 = 1000 (ii) 2^8 = 256 (iii) 3^(-3) = 1/27 (iv) 20^2 = 400 (v) 16^(-1/4) = 1/2 (vi) 11^2 = 121 (vii) p = q^r (viii) (32)^(-1/5) = 1/2

Formula: b^y = x is written in logarithmic form as log_b (x) = y (base b becomes the base of the log, exponent y becomes the answer).

(i) 10^3 = 1000: log_10 (1000) = 3.

(ii) 2^8 = 256: log_2 (256) = 8.

(iii) 3^(-3) = 1/27: log_3 (1/27) = -3.

(iv) 20^2 = 400: log_20 (400) = 2.

(v) 16^(-1/4) = 1/2: log_16 (1/2) = -1/4.

(vi) 11^2 = 121: log_11 (121) = 2.

(vii) p = q^r: Here the base is q and the exponent is r, so log_q (p) = r.

(viii) (32)^(-1/5) = 1/2: log_32 (1/2) = -1/5.

Q2: Express each of the following in exponential form

(i) log_5 (125) = 3 (ii) log_2 (16) = 4 (iii) log_23 (1) = 0 (iv) log_5 (5) = 1 (v) log_2 (1/8) = -3 (vi) 1/2 = log_9 (3) (vii) 5 = log_10 (100000) (viii) log_4 (1/16) = -2

Formula: log_b (x) = y is written in exponential form as b^y = x.

(i) log_5 (125) = 3: 5^3 = 125.

(ii) log_2 (16) = 4: 2^4 = 16.

(iii) log_23 (1) = 0: 23^0 = 1.

(iv) log_5 (5) = 1: 5^1 = 5.

(v) log_2 (1/8) = -3: 2^(-3) = 1/8.

(vi) 1/2 = log_9 (3): 9^(1/2) = 3.

(vii) 5 = log_10 (100000): 10^5 = 100000.

(viii) log_4 (1/16) = -2: 4^(-2) = 1/16.

Q3: Find the value of x in each of the following

(i) log_x (64) = 3 (ii) log_5 (1) = x (iii) log_x (8) = 1 (iv) log_10 (x) = -3 (v) log_4 (x) = 3/2 (vi) log_2 (1024) = x

Method: Change each equation to exponential form using Formula: log_b (x) = y means b^y = x, then compare powers.

(i) log_x (64) = 3: Step 1: x^3 = 64. Step 2: x^3 = 4^3. Step 3: x = 4.

(ii) log_5 (1) = x: Step 1: 5^x = 1. Step 2: 5^x = 5^0. Step 3: x = 0.

(iii) log_x (8) = 1: Step 1: x^1 = 8. Step 2: x = 8.

(iv) log_10 (x) = -3: Step 1: x = 10^(-3). Step 2: x = 1/1000 = 0.001.

(v) log_4 (x) = 3/2: Step 1: x = 4^(3/2). Step 2: x = (2^2)^(3/2) = 2^3 = 8.

(vi) log_2 (1024) = x: Step 1: 2^x = 1024. Step 2: 1024 = 2^10, so 2^x = 2^10. Step 3: x = 10.

mcqs.q: 2^8 = 256 in logarithmic form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: b^y = x is written as log_b (x) = y. Here the base is 2 and the exponent is 8, so log_2 (256) = 8.

mcqs.q: 3^(-3) = 1/27 in logarithmic form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: b^y = x means log_b (x) = y. The base is 3, the value is 1/27 and the exponent is -3, so log_3 (1/27) = -3.

mcqs.q: log_5 (125) = 3 in exponential form is:
mcqs.why: Formula: log_b (x) = y means b^y = x. The base 5 raised to the power 3 gives 125: 5^3 = 125.

mcqs.q: log_23 (1) = 0 because in exponential form:
mcqs.why: Formula: log_b (x) = y means b^y = x. Any non-zero base raised to the power 0 equals 1, so log of 1 is 0 for every base.

mcqs.q: If log_x (64) = 3, then x =
mcqs.why: Step 1: Exponential form: x^3 = 64. Step 2: 64 = 4^3, so x^3 = 4^3. Step 3: Comparing bases, x = 4.

mcqs.q: If log_4 (x) = 3/2, then x =
mcqs.why: Step 1: Exponential form: x = 4^(3/2). Step 2: 4 = 2^2, so x = (2^2)^(3/2) = 2^3. Step 3: x = 8.

mcqs.q: log_2 (1024) is equal to:
If log_10 (x) = -3, then x =
The exponential form of 1/2 = log_9 (3) is:
mcqs.why: Formula: log_b (x) = y means b^y = x. Here base 9, exponent 1/2, value 3: 9^(1/2) = sqrt(9) = 3.

mcqs.q: If log_x (8) = 1, then x =
mcqs.why: Step 1: Exponential form: x^1 = 8. Step 2: x = 8, since the logarithm of the base itself is always 1.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.3
lessons.notes_html:
Q1: Find the characteristic of the following numbers

(i) 5287 (ii) 59.28 (iii) 0.0567 (iv) 234.7 (v) 0.000049 (vi) 145000

Rules: Formula (number > 1): Characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point) - 1. Formula (number < 1): Characteristic = -(number of zeros between the decimal point and the first non-zero digit + 1), written with a bar.

(i) 5287: digits before the point = 4. Characteristic = 4 - 1 = 3.

(ii) 59.28: digits before the point = 2. Characteristic = 2 - 1 = 1.

(iii) 0.0567: zeros before the first non-zero digit = 1. Characteristic = -(1 + 1) = -2, i.e. 2 (bar).

(iv) 234.7: digits before the point = 3. Characteristic = 3 - 1 = 2.

(v) 0.000049: zeros before the first non-zero digit = 4. Characteristic = -(4 + 1) = -5, i.e. 5 (bar).

(vi) 145000: digits = 6. Characteristic = 6 - 1 = 5.

Q2: Find the logarithm of the following numbers (using the log table)

(i) 43 (ii) 579 (iii) 1.982 (iv) 0.0876 (v) 0.047 (vi) 0.000354

Formula: log (number) = Characteristic + Mantissa. The mantissa is read from the log table for the digits of the number; it is always positive.

(i) log 43: Step 1: Characteristic = 2 - 1 = 1. Step 2: Mantissa from the table (row 43, column 0) = 0.6335. Step 3: log 43 = 1 + 0.6335 = 1.6335.

(ii) log 579: Step 1: Characteristic = 3 - 1 = 2. Step 2: Mantissa (row 57, column 9) = 0.7627. Step 3: log 579 = 2 + 0.7627 = 2.7627.

(iii) log 1.982: Step 1: Characteristic = 1 - 1 = 0. Step 2: Mantissa (row 19, column 8, mean difference for 2) = 0.2971. Step 3: log 1.982 = 0 + 0.2971 = 0.2971.

(iv) log 0.0876: Step 1: Characteristic = -(1 + 1) = -2, i.e. 2 (bar). Step 2: Mantissa (row 87, column 6) = 0.9425. Step 3: log 0.0876 = -2 + 0.9425 = -1.0575, written as (bar 1).9425.

(v) log 0.047: Step 1: Characteristic = -(1 + 1) = -2, i.e. 2 (bar). Step 2: Mantissa (row 47, column 0) = 0.6721. Step 3: log 0.047 = -2 + 0.6721 = -1.3279, written as (bar 1).6721... in bar form: (bar 2) + 0.6721.

(vi) log 0.000354: Step 1: Characteristic = -(3 + 1) = -4, i.e. 4 (bar). Step 2: Mantissa (row 35, column 4) = 0.5490. Step 3: log 0.000354 = -4 + 0.5490 = -3.4510, i.e. (bar 4).5490.

Q3: If log 3.177 = 0.5019, then find

(i) log 3177 (ii) log 31.77 (iii) log 0.03177

Rule: Multiplying a number by 10^k adds k to the characteristic only; the mantissa stays the same, because the digit sequence 3177 is unchanged.

Given: log 3.177 = 0.5019 (characteristic 0, mantissa 0.5019).

(i) log 3177: Step 1: 3177 = 3.177 x 10^3. Step 2: Characteristic = 3. Step 3: log 3177 = 3 + 0.5019 = 3.5019.

(ii) log 31.77: Step 1: 31.77 = 3.177 x 10^1. Step 2: Characteristic = 1. Step 3: log 31.77 = 1 + 0.5019 = 1.5019.

(iii) log 0.03177: Step 1: 0.03177 = 3.177 x 10^(-2). Step 2: Characteristic = -2, i.e. 2 (bar). Step 3: log 0.03177 = -2 + 0.5019 = -1.4981, written (bar 2).5019.

Q4: Find the value of x

(i) log x = 0.0065 (ii) log x = 1.192 (iii) log x = -3.434 (iv) log x = -1.5726 (v) log x = 4.3561 (vi) log x = -2.0184

Method: x = antilog of the given logarithm. First write the logarithm as characteristic + positive mantissa, read the digits from the antilog table, then place the decimal point using the characteristic.

(i) log x = 0.0065: Step 1: Characteristic = 0, Mantissa = 0.0065. Step 2: Antilog digits for 0.0065 = 1015 (table). Step 3: Characteristic 0 means the point is after 1 digit: x = 1.015.

(ii) log x = 1.192: Step 1: Characteristic = 1, Mantissa = 0.192. Step 2: Antilog digits = 1556. Step 3: Characteristic 1 means the point is after 2 digits: x = 15.56.

(iii) log x = -3.434: Step 1: Make the mantissa positive: -3.434 = -4 + 0.566, i.e. (bar 4).5660. Step 2: Antilog digits for 0.5660 = 3681. Step 3: Characteristic -4 means three zeros after the point before the digits: x = 0.0003681.

(iv) log x = -1.5726: Step 1: -1.5726 = -2 + 0.4274, i.e. (bar 2).4274. Step 2: Antilog digits for 0.4274 = 2675. Step 3: Characteristic -2 means one zero after the point: x = 0.02675.

(v) log x = 4.3561: Step 1: Characteristic = 4, Mantissa = 0.3561. Step 2: Antilog digits = 2270. Step 3: Characteristic 4 means the point is after 5 digits: x = 22,700 (more precisely 22,704).

(vi) log x = -2.0184: Step 1: -2.0184 = -3 + 0.9816, i.e. (bar 3).9816. Step 2: Antilog digits for 0.9816 = 9585. Step 3: Characteristic -3 means two zeros after the point: x = 0.009585.

mcqs.q: The characteristic of 5287 is:
mcqs.why: Formula (number > 1): Characteristic = (digits before the decimal point) - 1. 5287 has 4 digits before the point, so the characteristic = 4 - 1 = 3.

mcqs.q: The characteristic of 0.0567 is:
mcqs.why: Formula (number < 1): Characteristic = -(zeros between the point and the first non-zero digit + 1). 0.0567 has 1 such zero, so the characteristic = -(1 + 1) = -2.

mcqs.q: The characteristic of 0.000049 is:
mcqs.why: There are 4 zeros between the decimal point and the first non-zero digit 4. Characteristic = -(4 + 1) = -5, written with a bar over 5.

mcqs.q: log 43 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Formula: log (number) = Characteristic + Mantissa. Step 1: Characteristic of 43 = 2 - 1 = 1. Step 2: Mantissa from the table for 43 = 0.6335. Step 3: log 43 = 1 + 0.6335 = 1.6335.

mcqs.q: If log 3.177 = 0.5019, then log 3177 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: 3177 = 3.177 x 10^3, so only the characteristic changes. Step 2: Characteristic = 3, mantissa stays 0.5019. Step 3: log 3177 = 3 + 0.5019 = 3.5019.

mcqs.q: If log 3.177 = 0.5019, then log 0.03177 is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: 0.03177 = 3.177 x 10^(-2). Step 2: The characteristic becomes -2 while the mantissa 0.5019 is unchanged. Step 3: log 0.03177 = -2 + 0.5019.

mcqs.q: If log x = 1.192, then x is approximately:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Characteristic = 1, mantissa = 0.192. Step 2: Antilog digits for 0.192 are 1556. Step 3: Characteristic 1 puts the point after 2 digits: x = 15.56.

mcqs.q: If log x = -3.434, then x is approximately:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write -3.434 = -4 + 0.566, i.e. characteristic -4, mantissa 0.5660. Step 2: Antilog digits = 3681. Step 3: Characteristic -4 means three zeros after the point before the digits: x = 0.0003681.

mcqs.q: In log (number) = characteristic + mantissa, the mantissa is always:
mcqs.why: The mantissa is read from the log table for the digit sequence and is always positive (between 0 and 1). Only the characteristic can be negative, which is why bar notation is used.

mcqs.q: log 0.0876 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Characteristic of 0.0876 = -(1 + 1) = -2. Step 2: Mantissa from the table for 876 = 0.9425. Step 3: log 0.0876 = -2 + 0.9425 = -1.0575.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.4
lessons.notes_html:
Q1: Without using a calculator, evaluate the following

(i) log_2 (18) - log_2 (9) (ii) log_2 (64) + log_2 (2) (iii) (1/3) log_3 (8) - log_3 (18) (iv) 2 log 2 + log 25 (v) (1/3) log_4 (64) + 2 log_5 (25) (vi) log_3 (12) + log_3 (0.25)

Laws used: Formula (Product): log_b (xy) = log_b x + log_b y. Formula (Quotient): log_b (x/y) = log_b x - log_b y. Formula (Power): log_b (x^n) = n log_b x.

(i) log_2 (18) - log_2 (9): Step 1: Quotient law: = log_2 (18/9) = log_2 (2). Step 2: log_2 (2) = 1 (because 2^1 = 2).

(ii) log_2 (64) + log_2 (2): Step 1: 64 = 2^6, so log_2 (64) = 6. Step 2: log_2 (2) = 1. Step 3: Sum = 6 + 1 = 7.

(iii) (1/3) log_3 (8) - log_3 (18): Step 1: Power law in reverse: (1/3) log_3 (8) = log_3 (8^(1/3)) = log_3 (2). Step 2: Quotient law: = log_3 (2/18) = log_3 (1/9). Step 3: 1/9 = 3^(-2), so = -2.

(iv) 2 log 2 + log 25: Step 1: Power law: 2 log 2 = log (2^2) = log 4. Step 2: Product law: = log 4 + log 25 = log (4 x 25) = log 100. Step 3: log 100 = 2 (because 10^2 = 100).

(v) (1/3) log_4 (64) + 2 log_5 (25): Step 1: 64 = 4^3, so log_4 (64) = 3 and (1/3)(3) = 1. Step 2: 25 = 5^2, so log_5 (25) = 2 and 2 x 2 = 4. Step 3: Sum = 1 + 4 = 5.

(vi) log_3 (12) + log_3 (0.25): Step 1: Product law: = log_3 (12 x 0.25) = log_3 (3). Step 2: log_3 (3) = 1.

Q2: Write the following as a single logarithm

(i) (1/2) log 25 + 2 log 3 (ii) log 9 - log (1/3) (iii) log_5 (b^2) - log_5 (5^3) (iv) 2 log_3 (x) + log_3 (y) (v) 4 log_5 (x) - log_5 (y) + log_5 (z) (vi) 2 ln a + 3 ln b - 4 ln c

Method: First use Formula (Power): n log x = log (x^n), then Formula (Product): log x + log y = log (xy) and Formula (Quotient): log x - log y = log (x/y).

(i) (1/2) log 25 + 2 log 3: Step 1: = log (25^(1/2)) + log (3^2) = log 5 + log 9. Step 2: = log (5 x 9) = log 45.

(ii) log 9 - log (1/3): Step 1: Quotient law: = log [9 / (1/3)]. Step 2: = log (9 x 3) = log 27.

(iii) log_5 (b^2) - log_5 (5^3) [see Note]: Step 1: Quotient law: = log_5 [b^2 / 5^3]. Step 2: = log_5 (b^2 / 125). Note: In the printed book this item is partly covered by the watermark; it is read as log_5 (b^2) - log_5 (5^3).

(iv) 2 log_3 (x) + log_3 (y): Step 1: = log_3 (x^2) + log_3 (y). Step 2: = log_3 (x^2 y).

(v) 4 log_5 (x) - log_5 (y) + log_5 (z): Step 1: = log_5 (x^4) - log_5 (y) + log_5 (z). Step 2: = log_5 (x^4 z / y).

(vi) 2 ln a + 3 ln b - 4 ln c: Step 1: = ln (a^2) + ln (b^3) - ln (c^4). Step 2: = ln (a^2 b^3 / c^4).

Q3: Expand the following using laws of logarithms

(i) log (11/5) (ii) log_5 sqrt(8 a^6) (iii) ln (a^2 b / c) (iv) log [(xy/z)^(1/9)] (v) ln [cube root of (16 x^3)] (vi) log_2 [((1 - a)/b)^5]

Laws used: Formula (Quotient): log (x/y) = log x - log y. Formula (Product): log (xy) = log x + log y. Formula (Power): log (x^n) = n log x; a root is a fractional power.

(i) log (11/5): = log 11 - log 5.

(ii) log_5 sqrt(8 a^6): Step 1: sqrt(8 a^6) = (8 a^6)^(1/2). Step 2: = (1/2) log_5 (8 a^6). Step 3: = (1/2)[log_5 (8) + log_5 (a^6)] = (1/2) log_5 (8) + (1/2)(6 log_5 a) = (1/2) log_5 (8) + 3 log_5 (a).

(iii) ln (a^2 b / c): = ln (a^2) + ln (b) - ln (c) = 2 ln a + ln b - ln c.

(iv) log [(xy/z)^(1/9)]: Step 1: Power law: = (1/9) log (xy/z). Step 2: = (1/9)[log x + log y - log z].

(v) ln [cube root of (16 x^3)]: Step 1: cube root = power 1/3: = (1/3) ln (16 x^3). Step 2: = (1/3)[ln 16 + ln (x^3)] = (1/3) ln 16 + (1/3)(3 ln x) = (1/3) ln 16 + ln x.

(vi) log_2 [((1 - a)/b)^5]: Step 1: Power law: = 5 log_2 ((1 - a)/b). Step 2: Quotient law: = 5 [log_2 (1 - a) - log_2 (b)].

Q4: Find the value of x in the following equations

(i) log 2 + log x = 1 (ii) log_2 (x) + log_2 (8) = 5 (iii) (81)^x = (243)^(x+2) (iv) (1/27)^(x-6) = 27 (v) log (5x - 10) = 2 (vi) log_2 (x + 1) - log_2 (x - 4) = 2

(i) log 2 + log x = 1: Step 1: Product law: log (2x) = 1. Step 2: Exponential form: 2x = 10^1 = 10. Step 3: x = 10/2 = 5.

(ii) log_2 (x) + log_2 (8) = 5: Step 1: Product law: log_2 (8x) = 5. Step 2: Exponential form: 8x = 2^5 = 32. Step 3: x = 32/8 = 4.

(iii) (81)^x = (243)^(x+2): Step 1: Write both sides as powers of 3: 81 = 3^4 and 243 = 3^5, so 3^(4x) = 3^(5x + 10). Step 2: Equate exponents: 4x = 5x + 10. Step 3: 4x - 5x = 10, so -x = 10. Step 4: x = -10.

(iv) (1/27)^(x-6) = 27: Step 1: 1/27 = 3^(-3) and 27 = 3^3, so 3^[-3(x-6)] = 3^3. Step 2: Equate exponents: -3(x - 6) = 3. Step 3: -3x + 18 = 3, so -3x = 3 - 18 = -15. Step 4: x = 5.

(v) log (5x - 10) = 2: Step 1: Exponential form: 5x - 10 = 10^2 = 100. Step 2: 5x = 100 + 10 = 110. Step 3: x = 110/5 = 22.

(vi) log_2 (x + 1) - log_2 (x - 4) = 2: Step 1: Quotient law: log_2 [(x + 1)/(x - 4)] = 2. Step 2: Exponential form: (x + 1)/(x - 4) = 2^2 = 4. Step 3: x + 1 = 4(x - 4) = 4x - 16. Step 4: 1 + 16 = 4x - x, so 17 = 3x. Step 5: x = 17/3.

Q5: Find the values of the following with the help of the logarithm table

(i) (3.68 x 4.21) / 5.234 (ii) 4.67 x 2.11 x 2.397 (iii) [(20.46)^2 x 2.4122] / 754.3 (iv) [cube root of (9.364) x 21.64] / 3.21

Method: Take log of the whole expression, use the laws of logarithms with table values, then take the antilog. Table values used: log 3.68 = 0.5658, log 4.21 = 0.6243, log 5.234 = 0.7188, log 4.67 = 0.6693, log 2.11 = 0.3243, log 2.397 = 0.3797, log 20.46 = 1.3109, log 2.4122 = 0.3824, log 754.3 = 2.8775, log 9.364 = 0.9715, log 21.64 = 1.3353, log 3.21 = 0.5065.

(i) Let x = (3.68 x 4.21) / 5.234. Step 1: log x = log 3.68 + log 4.21 - log 5.234 (product and quotient laws). Step 2: = 0.5658 + 0.6243 - 0.7188 = 0.4713. Step 3: x = antilog (0.4713) = 2.960.

(ii) Let x = 4.67 x 2.11 x 2.397. Step 1: log x = log 4.67 + log 2.11 + log 2.397. Step 2: = 0.6693 + 0.3243 + 0.3797 = 1.3733. Step 3: x = antilog (1.3733) = 23.62.

(iii) Let x = [(20.46)^2 x 2.4122] / 754.3. Step 1: log x = 2 log 20.46 + log 2.4122 - log 754.3 (power, product, quotient laws). Step 2: = 2(1.3109) + 0.3824 - 2.8775 = 2.6218 + 0.3824 - 2.8775 = 0.1267. Step 3: x = antilog (0.1267) = 1.339.

(iv) Let x = [cube root of (9.364) x 21.64] / 3.21. Step 1: log x = (1/3) log 9.364 + log 21.64 - log 3.21. Step 2: = (1/3)(0.9715) + 1.3353 - 0.5065 = 0.3238 + 1.3353 - 0.5065 = 1.1526. Step 3: x = antilog (1.1526) = 14.21.

Q6

The formula to measure the magnitude of earthquakes is M = log_10 (A / A_o). If amplitude (A) is 10,000 and reference amplitude (A_o) is 10, what is the magnitude of the earthquake?

Step 1: Formula: M = log_10 (A / A_o), with A = 10,000 and A_o = 10.

Step 2: A / A_o = 10,000 / 10 = 1000.

Step 3: M = log_10 (1000).

Step 4: 1000 = 10^3, so M = 3.

Hence the magnitude of the earthquake is 3.

Q7

Abdullah invested Rs. 100,000 in a saving scheme and gains interest at the rate of 5% per annum so that the total value of this investment after t years is Rs. y. This is modelled by the equation y = 100,000 (1.05)^t, t >= 0. Find after how many years the investment will be double.

Step 1: The investment doubles when y = 2 x 100,000 = 200,000. Put y = 200,000 in y = 100,000 (1.05)^t.

Step 2: 200,000 = 100,000 (1.05)^t, so (1.05)^t = 2.

Step 3: Take log of both sides: t log (1.05) = log 2. Formula: log (x^n) = n log x.

Step 4: t = log 2 / log 1.05 = 0.3010 / 0.0212 = 14.21.

Hence the investment will be double after about 14.2 years.

Q8

Huria is hiking up a mountain where the temperature (T) decreases by 3% (or a factor of 0.97) for every 100 metres gained in altitude. The initial temperature (T_i) at sea level is 20 degrees C. Using the formula T = T_i x 0.97^(h/100), calculate the temperature at an altitude (h) of 500 metres.

Step 1: Formula: T = T_i x 0.97^(h/100), with T_i = 20 and h = 500.

Step 2: h/100 = 500/100 = 5.

Step 3: T = 20 x (0.97)^5.

Step 4: (0.97)^5 = 0.8587 (by repeated multiplication: 0.97^2 = 0.9409, 0.97^4 = 0.8853, 0.97^5 = 0.8853 x 0.97 = 0.8587).

Step 5: T = 20 x 0.8587 = 17.17.

Hence the temperature at 500 metres is about 17.17 degrees C.

mcqs.why: Step 1: Quotient law: log_b x - log_b y = log_b (x/y), so = log_2 (18/9) = log_2 (2). Step 2: log_2 (2) = 1 because 2^1 = 2.

mcqs.q: log_2 (64) + log_2 (2) is equal to:
2 log 2 + log 25 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Power law: 2 log 2 = log (2^2) = log 4. Step 2: Product law: log 4 + log 25 = log (4 x 25) = log 100. Step 3: log 100 = 2 because 10^2 = 100.

mcqs.q: (1/2) log 25 + 2 log 3 as a single logarithm is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Power law: (1/2) log 25 = log (25^(1/2)) = log 5, and 2 log 3 = log (3^2) = log 9. Step 2: Product law: log 5 + log 9 = log (5 x 9) = log 45.

mcqs.q: log 9 - log (1/3) as a single logarithm is:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Quotient law: log x - log y = log (x/y), so = log [9 / (1/3)]. Step 2: 9 / (1/3) = 9 x 3 = 27. Result = log 27.

mcqs.q: The expansion of log (11/5) is:
mcqs.why: Quotient law: log (x/y) = log x - log y. With x = 11 and y = 5, log (11/5) = log 11 - log 5.

mcqs.q: If log 2 + log x = 1, then x =
mcqs.why: Step 1: Product law: log (2x) = 1. Step 2: Exponential form: 2x = 10^1 = 10. Step 3: x = 10/2 = 5.

mcqs.q: If log (5x - 10) = 2, then x =
mcqs.why: Step 1: Exponential form: 5x - 10 = 10^2 = 100. Step 2: 5x = 100 + 10 = 110. Step 3: x = 110/5 = 22.

mcqs.q: With M = log_10 (A / A_o), A = 10,000 and A_o = 10, the earthquake magnitude M is:
An investment doubles under y = 100,000 (1.05)^t after about:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Doubling gives (1.05)^t = 2. Step 2: Take logs: t log (1.05) = log 2. Step 3: t = log 2 / log 1.05 = 0.3010 / 0.0212 = 14.21, about 14.2 years.

Q1 (x)

3^4 = 81 in logarithmic form is:
(a) log_3 (4) = 81   (b) log_4 (3) = 81   (c) log_3 (81) = 4   (d) log_4 (81) = 3
Correct answer: log_3 (81) = 4

Q2: Express the following numbers in scientific notation

(i) 0.000567 (ii) 734 (iii) 0.33 x 10^3

Rule: a x 10^n with 1 <= a < 10.

(i) 0.000567: Move the point 4 places right: 5.67. = 5.67 x 10^(-4).

(ii) 734: Move the point 2 places left: 7.34. = 7.34 x 10^2.

(iii) 0.33 x 10^3: Step 1: 0.33 = 3.3 x 10^(-1). Step 2: = 3.3 x 10^(-1+3) = 3.3 x 10^2.

Q3: Express the following numbers in ordinary notation

(i) 2.6 x 10^3 (ii) 8.794 x 10^(-4) (iii) 6 x 10^(-6)

(i) 2.6 x 10^3: Move the point 3 places right: = 2600.

(ii) 8.794 x 10^(-4): Move the point 4 places left: = 0.0008794.

(iii) 6 x 10^(-6): Move the point 6 places left: = 0.000006.

Q4: Express each of the following in logarithmic form

(i) 3^7 = 2187 (ii) a^b = c (iii) (12)^2 = 144

Formula: b^y = x means log_b (x) = y.

(i) 3^7 = 2187: log_3 (2187) = 7.

(ii) a^b = c: log_a (c) = b.

(iii) (12)^2 = 144: log_12 (144) = 2.

Q5: Express each of the following in exponential form

(i) log_8 (8) = x (ii) log_9 (729) = 3 (iii) log_4 (1024) = 5

Formula: log_b (x) = y means b^y = x.

(i) log_8 (8) = x: 8^x = 8 (so x = 1).

(ii) log_9 (729) = 3: 9^3 = 729.

(iii) log_4 (1024) = 5: 4^5 = 1024.

Q6: Find the value of x in the following

(i) log_9 (x) = 0.5 (ii) (1/9)^(3x) = 27 (iii) (1/32)^(2x) = 64

(i) log_9 (x) = 0.5: Step 1: Exponential form: x = 9^(0.5). Step 2: x = sqrt(9) = 3.

(ii) (1/9)^(3x) = 27: Step 1: 1/9 = 3^(-2) and 27 = 3^3, so 3^(-6x) = 3^3. Step 2: Equate exponents: -6x = 3. Step 3: x = -1/2.

(iii) (1/32)^(2x) = 64: Step 1: 1/32 = 2^(-5) and 64 = 2^6, so 2^(-10x) = 2^6. Step 2: Equate exponents: -10x = 6. Step 3: x = -6/10 = -3/5.

Q7: Write the following as a single logarithm

(i) 7 log x - 3 log (y^2) (ii) 3 log 4 - log 32 (iii) (1/3)(log_5 (8) + log_5 (27)) - log_5 (3)

Laws: Formula (Power): n log x = log (x^n); Formula (Product): log x + log y = log (xy); Formula (Quotient): log x - log y = log (x/y).

(i) 7 log x - 3 log (y^2): Step 1: 3 log (y^2) = log [(y^2)^3] = log (y^6) and 7 log x = log (x^7). Step 2: = log (x^7 / y^6).

(ii) 3 log 4 - log 32: Step 1: = log (4^3) - log 32 = log 64 - log 32. Step 2: = log (64/32) = log 2.

(iii) (1/3)(log_5 (8) + log_5 (27)) - log_5 (3): Step 1: Product law inside: log_5 (8) + log_5 (27) = log_5 (216). Step 2: (1/3) log_5 (216) = log_5 (216^(1/3)) = log_5 (6). Step 3: = log_5 (6) - log_5 (3) = log_5 (6/3) = log_5 (2).

Q8: Expand the following using laws of logarithms

(i) log (x y z^6) (ii) log_3 [6th root of (m^5 n^3)] (iii) log sqrt(8 x^3)

(i) log (x y z^6): Product and power laws: = log x + log y + log (z^6) = log x + log y + 6 log z.

(ii) log_3 [6th root of (m^5 n^3)]: Step 1: 6th root = power 1/6: = (1/6) log_3 (m^5 n^3). Step 2: = (1/6)[5 log_3 (m) + 3 log_3 (n)] = (5/6) log_3 (m) + (1/2) log_3 (n).

(iii) log sqrt(8 x^3): Step 1: sqrt = power 1/2: = (1/2) log (8 x^3). Step 2: = (1/2)[log 8 + 3 log x] = (1/2) log 8 + (3/2) log x.

Q9: Find the values of the following with the help of the logarithm table

(i) cube root of (68.24) (ii) 319.8 x 3.543 (iii) (36.12 x 750.9) / (113.2 x 9.98)

Method: Take log, use the laws with table values, then take antilog. Table values: log 68.24 = 1.8340, log 319.8 = 2.5049, log 3.543 = 0.5494, log 36.12 = 1.5577, log 750.9 = 2.8756, log 113.2 = 2.0538, log 9.98 = 0.9991.

(i) Let x = cube root of (68.24). Step 1: log x = (1/3) log 68.24 = (1/3)(1.8340) = 0.6113. Step 2: x = antilog (0.6113) = 4.086.

(ii) Let x = 319.8 x 3.543. Step 1: log x = log 319.8 + log 3.543 = 2.5049 + 0.5494 = 3.0543. Step 2: x = antilog (3.0543) = 1133 (more precisely 1133.05).

(iii) Let x = (36.12 x 750.9) / (113.2 x 9.98). Step 1: log x = log 36.12 + log 750.9 - log 113.2 - log 9.98. Step 2: = 1.5577 + 2.8756 - 2.0538 - 0.9991 = 1.3804. Step 3: x = antilog (1.3804) = 24.01.

Q10

In the year 2016, the population of a city was 22 millions and was growing at a rate of 2.5% per year. The function p(t) = 22 (1.025)^t gives the population in millions, t years after 2016. Use the model to determine in which year the population will reach 35 millions. Round the answer to the nearest year.

Step 1: Put p(t) = 35 in p(t) = 22 (1.025)^t: 35 = 22 (1.025)^t.

Step 2: (1.025)^t = 35/22 = 1.5909.

Step 3: Take log of both sides: t log (1.025) = log (1.5909). Formula: log (x^n) = n log x.

Step 4: t = log (1.5909) / log (1.025) = 0.2016 / 0.0107 = 18.8.

Step 5: Rounded to the nearest year, t = 19 years after 2016.

Hence the population will reach 35 millions in the year 2016 + 19 = 2035.

mcqs.q: The expansion of log (x y z^6) is:
